page: Microsoft Azure F1as_v7 is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 1 vCPU corresponding to 1 physical core and 1 thread, supplemented by 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 4.0 GB of system memory, with no GPUs present and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent storage operations.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded performance contrasted by strict multi-threaded ceilings due to its single-core limitation. In stress-ng single-core tests, the F1as_v7 reaches the top 10% tier with 3750.28 points. Similarly, single-threaded compression benchmarks demonstrate exceptional capability, reaching 40.93 GB/sec in gzip compression and 18.11 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, both falling in the top 10% tier. Modern vector instructions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 are fully supported, alongside cryptographic accelerators like AES and SHA-NI.

Because the VM is restricted to a single vCPU, aggregate throughput scores are constrained. Multi-core stress-ng, PassMark CPU (3461.72), PassMark memory (1616.57), and PassMark database operations (1469.75) rank in the bottom 25%. Network and serving capacities are similarly modest, yielding 2.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 3.75 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth is average, recording 41.98 GB/sec read and 32.1 GB/sec write. Lightweight LLM inference on small 135M parameter models runs at an average tier of 423.47 tokens per second for prompt processing and 179.91 tokens per second for text generation.

Qualitatively, the F1as_v7 offers a low barrier to entry for workloads prioritizing raw single-thread clock speed over parallel scaling. It is best matched for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight automation, low-concurrency web serving, and continuous integration task runners that benefit from the 4.5 GHz core frequency.
description: Microsoft Azure F1as_v7 is a single-core, compute-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.5 GHz dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 1 vCPU, 4.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware. Benchmarks show top-tier single-threaded capability, achieving 3750.28 in stress-ng single-core tests and over 40 GB/sec in gzip compression, supported by advanced vector extensions like AVX-512. However, overall system capacity is constrained by the single-core topology, with multi-core metrics, database operations, and web throughput scoring in the lower quartile. The F1as_v7 represents a cost-effective choice for lightweight single-threaded tasks, simple batch jobs, and low-scale web services requiring high per-core clock frequency.
